newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-COUPLES WINS SECOND STRAIGHT SKINS GAME TITLE, $280,000.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-COUPLES WINS SECOND STRAIGHT SKINS GAME TITLE, $280,000.

text.p: Fred Couples sank a $240,000 birdie putt Sunday to win his second straight Skins Game title at the Rancho La Quinta Country Club.

Couples became the first player in the 14-year history of the Skins Game to surpass $1 million in earnings when he rolled in an eight-foot birdie at the par-4 15th hole. It boosted his winnings at the two-day, made-for-TV event to $280,000 -- $60,000 more than veteran Tom Watson.

"It wasn't the greatest feat in the world, but it was fun," said Couples, who had a stellar year financially although he won only once on the PGA Tour. "They all played better than I did. I felt like I played fair. Tom and Tiger tied every hole and I got the money."

Couples, who has $1,190,000 in career Skins Game earnings, became the first back-to-back winner since Payne Stewart captured the event from 1991-93. Fuzzy Zoeller also successfully defended his championship 11 years ago.

The 47-year-old Watson was the only other player to win a skin on the second day, birdying the second playoff hole worth $120,000. The 1994 Skins Game winner fared much better than last year, when he was held without a skin.

"When the money started to build and add up, the talk got quieter," Watson said. "The faces got serious. Sure, I got nervous. It's a lot of money out there. That's the Skins Game, it's all timing. It's like everything else in life."
Twenty-year-old Tiger Woods won two skins and $40,000 on Saturday in his first Skins Game appearance. John Daly consistently outdrove his opponents, but was shut out in the weekend competition.

"At least I was consistent -- I didn't make one putt," Daly joked. "Nothing broke for me all day. When you're playing in the Skins Game, you don't want to be the one with no skins. I never felt comfortable with any of my putts today. It's just a matter of a lack of confidence."

Each hole represents a skin. Holes 1-6 were worth $20,000, holes 7-12 were worth $30,000 and holes 13-18 were worth $40,000. A player must win a hole to capture the skin and the money. If there is no winner, the money carries over to the next hole.
That's what happened to produce Couples' big payoff at number 15.

Players halved six straight holes, beginning Saturday at the par-five ninth. The money kept building until Couples hit his drive into the middle of the 15th fairway, 105 yards from the pin. He used a sand wedge to get within eight feet and birdied while Daly missed a seven-footer that would have halved the hole.

The final three holes were halved, as was the first playoff hole, but Watson came away with the final skin with a five-foot birdie. Woods pulled his 15-foot birdie attempt left, while Daly recovered from a bad drive only to leave a 20-foot birdie putt on the edge of the cup.
The Rancho La Quinta Country Club is a par-71 layout that measures 6,992 yards.
